newsitem.title: USA: ICI tells NASD it opposes bond fund risk ratings.
newsitem.headline: ICI tells NASD it opposes bond fund risk ratings.

text.p: Investment Company Institute will tell National Association of Securities Dealers on Monday that it strongly opposes the use of bond mutual fund risk ratings in sales literature given to customers, a spokesman said.

Standard & Poor's Ratings Group in 1994 launched a service to rate the risk of bond funds, including municipal funds. But NASD, which regulates mutual fund advertising, ruled that funds may not use such ratings in sales literature.
NASD worried that the ratings could mislead investors because they hinge on "assumptions and speculation" about the economy in general and about a company's solvency.
Nevertheless, NASD reopened the issue in December by calling for a new round of comments, due Feb 24.

ICI, a trade group for the mutual fund industry, will tell NASD in written comments later on Monday that rating agencies only should be in the business of rating past, not future, performance, said ICI spokesman John Collins.

Moreover, risk ratings are subjective, and they would not necessarily be accurate for all bond funds or fund investors, Collins, managing director of public information at ICI, said in a telephone interview.

For example, while a certain bond fund may be entirely appropriate for young people investing for the long term, the same fund would not be right for an older investor trying to avoid all volatility, Collins said.
Risk ratings also may confuse investors and they might be viewed by some buyers as a shortcut to reading the rest of the sales literature, Collins said.
If NASD were to proceed with ratings, then rating agenices should disclose how they reached the ratings and what the ratings do and do not tell investors, Collins said.
